If not, log warning.\\n#   * convergence: EM should converge in \u2264 200 iterations; record iters.\\n#\\n# Output: artifacts/method_out.json includes:\\n#   theta            : list length 5, in canonical order\\n#   alpha            : list length 250\\n#   beta             : list length 250, each inner list length 2\\n#   model_order      : list of 5 model identifiers\\n#   dropped_items    : list of cluster_ids with \u03b1 < 0\\n#   fit_diagnostics  : {iters, log_likelihood, condition_number}\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 5: Validation A \u2014 Correlation with Published Accuracy\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Compile a baseline table from authoritative public sources\\n# (HELM leaderboard, Open LLM Leaderboard v2, original model papers):\\n#\\n#   model_id                        | MMLU acc (5-shot) | HELM acc |\\n#   --------------------------------|-------------------|----------|\\n#   openai/gpt-4o-mini              | \u2248 0.82            | \u2248 0.79   |\\n#   anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku      | \u2248 0.78            | \u2248 0.76   |\\n#   meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b         | \u2248 0.68            | \u2248 0.65   |\\n#   qwen/qwen-2.5-7b                | \u2248 0.71            | \u2248 0.69   |\\n#   mistralai/mistral-7b            | \u2248 0.62            | \u2248 0.60   |\\n#\\n# (These are approximate; the executor MUST verify via HELM, Open-LLM\\n#  Leaderboard, and original release notes and replace the table with\\n#  real values. Provide URL and retrieval date for each.)\\n#\\n# Compute Pearson r between \u03b8_j and MMLU acc (and HELM acc) with\\n# 95% CI via Fisher z-transform. Bootstrapped CI over 10,000 resamples\\n# as a robustness check.\\n# Success: Pearson r > 0.85 with 95% CI lower bound > 0.65.\\n#\\n# Output: validation_table.json with r, CI, scatter plot spec.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 6: Validation B \u2014 Contamination Simulation\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Hypothesis: a model that memorizes seed answers (but not the\\n# metamorphic variants) will see its static accuracy rise while its\\n# M-IRT \u03b8 holds or falls.\\n#\\n# Procedure (3 random seeds, e.g., 0/1/42):\\n#   1. Pick the middle-capability model (qwen-2.5-7b-instruct).\\n#   2. For a random 30% of seed items (75 clusters):\\n#        resp_sim(model, seed) := oracle_correct(seed)\\n#        (i.e., overwrite response with the canonical answer)\\n#      Leave all paraphrase/negation/contrapositive responses untouched\\n#      (these reflect the model's actual reasoning, broken on purpose).\\n#   3. Recompute:\\n#        static_acc_sim = mean over (simulated seed == oracle)\\n#        coherence_sim   = ordinal score with simulated seed, original others\\n#   4. Refit GRM on the full 5 \u00d7 250 matrix (4 models untouched,\\n#      target model = simulated profile). Extract \u03b8_sim for the target.\\n#   5. Repeat for the other 2 random seeds.\\n#\\n# Expected outcomes (success criteria):\\n#   * static_acc increases by \u2265 0.15 absolute (75 items forced correct)\\n#   * \u03b8_sim decreases OR stays within \u00b10.1 of \u03b8_clean (NOT statistically\\n#     distinguishable from zero) across all 3 seeds\\n#   * p-value (paired t-test on \u03b8_clean vs \u03b8_sim across seeds) > 0.05\\n#     for the null \\\"\u03b8 does not decrease\\\"\\n#\\n# Output: contamination_report.json with per-seed (static_acc_clean,\\n# static_acc_sim, theta_clean, theta_sim) plus the 3-seed mean.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Orchestration & Budget Enforcement\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# pipeline.py (entry point):\\n#   * parses CLI args (--stage, --seed, --n-clusters, --models)\\n#   * loads env (OPENROUTER_API_KEY from .env)\\n#   * calls each stage in order with @logger.catch(reraise=True)\\n#   * enforces hard budget: cumulative OpenRouter spend tracked in\\n#     artifacts/logs/spend.jsonl; raises if exceeds $3\\n#   * writes final method_out.json conforming to the repo schema\\n#   * prints a one-screen summary: \u03b8 ranking, r with MMLU, contamination\\n#     effect size\\n#\\n# Failure modes & mitigations:\\n#   * girth API drift \u2192 fall back to pyirt (Python IRT, has GRM via\\n#     pyirt.scorer.GradedResponse) or hand-rolled MML with scipy.stats.norm\\n#     + numpy outer products. Hand-rolled path documented in fallback_plan.\\n#   * OpenRouter rate limits \u2192 exponential backoff with tenacity,\\n#     reduce concurrency to Semaphore(10) on sustained 429s.\\n#   * Model deprecation \u2192 script accepts --model-override map; the\\n#     recommended substitutes are documented in fallback_plan.\\n#   * Budget overrun \u2192 halt after any single call that pushes spend >\\n#     $2.50; abort above $3.00 with a clear error.\\n#   * Cluster generation failures \u2192 if oracle validation drops below\\n#     90%, regenerate clusters from scratch with a FP_BLOCK_PLACEHOLDER_OLD\n  \\\"testing_plan\\\": \\\"TESTING_CONTENT_MARKER\\n  \\\"fallback_plan\\\": \\\"FP_START_PLACEHOLDER_FP_END\\\",\\n  \\\"testing_plan\\\": \\\"TP_START_PLACEHOLDER_TP_END\\\"\n# FALLBACK PLAN_INSERTED\\n#         pyirt.estimation.estimation_engine(...) . Same data shape.\\n#   * If a model ID is deprecated, swap via --model-override:\\n#         gpt-4o-mini        -> openai/gpt-4.1-mini\\n#         claude-3-5-haiku   -> anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5\\n#         llama-3.1-8b       -> meta-llama/llama-3.2-3b-instruct\\n#         qwen-2.5-7b        -> qwen/qwen-2.5-14b-instruct\\n#         mistral-7b         -> mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct\\n#     Re-run HELM/MMLU baseline lookup for the substituted model.\\n#\\n# TIER 2 \u2014 Hand-rolled GRM (if both libraries fail; ~30 min):\\n#   * Implement GRM from scratch in ~80 lines of NumPy:\\n#         P(X=k|\u03b8,\u03b1,\u03b2) = logistic(\u03b1(\u03b8-\u03b2_k)) -\\n#                          logistic(\u03b1(\u03b8-\u03b2_{k+1}))\\n#     with \u03b2_0 = -inf, \u03b2_K = +inf.\\n#   * Marginal likelihood for item i:\\n#         L_i(\u03b1_i, \u03b2_i | x_i) = sum_j \u222b P(x_ij | \u03b8_j) d\u03a6(\u03b8_j; 0, 1)\\n#     approximated by Gauss-Hermite quadrature with Q = 21 nodes.\\n#   * EM: E-step computes posterior weights w_{ij} for each \u03b8-quadrature\\n#         node; M-step updates \u03b1, \u03b2 by L-BFGS-B on the marginal log-likelihood.\\n#   * Stopping rule: |\u0394logL| < 1e-4 or 200 iterations.\\n#   * Output identical schema to girth result.\\n#   * Reference: Baker & Kim (2004), \\\"Item Response Theory: Parameter\\n#     Estimation Techniques\\\", 2nd ed., ch. 5.\\n#\\n# TIER 3 \u2014 Degraded scope (if budget exhausted or pipeline stalls):\\n#   * Drop the LLM-paraphrase pass entirely (Stage 1 \u00a7LLM paraphrase).\\n#     Rely on deterministic noun-swap paraphrases only.\\n#   * Reduce cluster count from 250 \u2192 100 (50 per domain).\\n#   * Reduce model panel from 5 \u2192 3 (drop llama-3.1-8b and mistral-7b,\\n#     keep one tier from low/mid/high).\\n#   * Skip Validation B (contamination) and report Validation A only.\\n#     Document the degradation explicitly in the output's\\n#     \\\"scope_limitations\\\" field.\\n#   * Pearson r target relaxes to r > 0.70 for the 3-model panel.\\n#\\n# Additional safeguards:\\n#   * If OpenRouter cost exceeds $2.50 cumulative, the script logs a\\n#     CRITICAL warning and switches remaining calls to the cheapest\\n#     available model in the panel (gpt-4o-mini or equivalent) only for\\n#     paraphrase validation, then halts at $3.00 with a clear error code.\\n#   * If coherence scoring yields < 3 items per response category for\\n#     any model (sparse data), refuse to fit GRM and report item\\n#     distribution histograms instead.\\n#   * If contamination simulation's t-test is undefined (zero variance),\\n#     fall back to reporting per-seed point estimates only.\",\n  \"testing_plan\": \"# =============================================================\\n# TESTING PLAN (gradual scale-up, per aii-long-running-tasks)\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Time budget: 6h. Use mini \u2192 10 \u2192 50 \u2192 100 \u2192 200 \u2192 250 scaling.\\n# At each stage: validate output shape, check for crashes, record\\n# runtime, then extrapolate before scaling further.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage A: Generation (CPU-only, no API spend) ----------\\n#\\n# A.1 (5 min) \u2014 MINI: generate 4 MICs (2 logic + 2 arithmetic) by hand\\n#   to verify the templating code paths execute end-to-end.\\n#   Checks:\\n#     * All 4 variants per cluster present\\n#     * Each variant has an oracle answer\\n#     * relations dict consistent\\n#   Stop criterion: passes if all 4 clusters pass.\\n#\\n# A.2 (10 min) \u2014 10 MICs: generate 5 logic + 5 arithmetic. Run oracle\\n#   validation on all 10. Checks: 100% pass.\\n#\\n# A.3 (10 min) \u2014 50 MICs: stress templating with all 12 logic + 8\\n#   arithmetic templates, varying nouns/items. Run oracle validation on\\n#   20% sample. Checks: \u2265 95% pass; if < 90%, fix templates.\\n#\\n# A.4 (15 min) \u2014 Full 250 MICs. Run oracle validation on 50 (20%).\\n#   Checks: \u2265 95% pass; persist to exp_gen_sol_out.json.\\n#   Record: total generation time, # MICs per template, slot-fill diversity.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage B: Model queries (API spend begins) ----------\\n#\\n# B.1 (5 min) \u2014 Smoke test: 1 model (gpt-4o-mini) \u00d7 4 MICs.\\n#   Checks:\\n#     * HTTP 200 response from OpenRouter\\n#     * Response token length \u2264 4 (one of {V, I, integer})\\n#     * Cost ledger records the call\\n#   If parse failures, add response normalization regex\\n#   r\\\"^\\\\s*([VvIi]|[-+]?\\\\d+)\\\" and retry.\\n#\\n# B.2 (15 min) \u2014 10 MICs \u00d7 1 model \u00d7 4 variants = 40 calls.\\n#   Checks: response normalization catches > 95% of outputs.\\n#   Compute coherence scores; verify at least one cluster scores 2\\n#   (i.e., the pipeline can produce non-degenerate scores).\\n#\\n# B.3 (30 min) \u2014 50 MICs \u00d7 1 model. Estimate cost per cluster.\\n#   Extrapolate: cost_per_cluster \u00d7 250 \u00d7 5 = total estimate.\\n#   Should be \u2264 $0.60.\\n#\\n# B.4 (60 min) \u2014 All 5 models \u00d7 100 MICs. Compute coherence for all.\\n#   Check rank ordering is non-degenerate (at least 2 distinct scores).\\n#\\n# B.5 (90 min) \u2014 All 5 models \u00d7 250 MICs \u00d7 4 variants = 5,000 calls.\\n#   Validate full response matrix populated; cumulative spend \u2264 $1.00.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage C: GRM fitting (CPU, ~minutes) ----------\\n#\\n# C.1 \u2014 Fit girth GRM on the (5, 250) matrix. Checks:\\n#     * Convergence in < 200 EM iterations\\n#     * All \u03b8_j finite and ordered (gpt-4o-mini > mistral-7b likely)\\n#     * Mean \u03b1_i > 0\\n#   If girth fails, attempt pyirt fallback; if both fail, run\\n#   hand-rolled NumPy GRM (Tier 2 of fallback plan).\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage D: Validation A (CPU) ----------\\n#\\n# D.1 \u2014 Verify the 5-model baseline accuracy table against HELM /\\n#   Open LLM Leaderboard (record retrieval date and source URL).\\n# D.2 \u2014 Compute Pearson r and bootstrap CI. Success: r > 0.85.\\n#   If not, diagnose:\\n#     * Inspect per-model \u03b8: is the ordering consistent with MMLU?\\n#     * Check item dropouts due to \u03b1 < 0; refit without them.\\n#     * Stratify by domain: report r_logic and r_arith separately.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage E: Validation B (contamination) ----------\\n#\\n# E.1 \u2014 Run contamination simulation on qwen-2.5-7b-instruct with\\n#   3 random seeds. Checks:\\n#     * static_acc_sim - static_acc_clean \u2265 0.15 on every seed\\n#     * |\u03b8_sim - \u03b8_clean| \u2264 0.3 (preferrably < 0.1) on every seed\\n#     * Per-seed report populated.\\n#   If static_acc does NOT rise, the contamination injection is\\n#   broken \u2014 debug the overwrite logic.\\n#   If \u03b8_sim RISES by more than 0.3, inspect whether GRM is overfitting\\n#   on the simulated profile; consider increasing item count or using\\n#   a regularization variant (e.g., EAP estimation instead of MML).\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage F: Final assembly ----------\\n#\\n# F.1 \u2014 Run the entire pipeline once more from scratch (mini \u2192 full)\\n#   to confirm reproducibility; verify identical \u03b8 and r within\\n#   tolerance (|\u0394\u03b8| < 0.05, |\u0394r| < 0.02).\\n# F.2 \u2014 Validate method_out.json against the repo schema (aii-json).\\n# F.3 \u2014 Print final summary table:\\n#   model | MMLU_acc | HELM_acc | \u03b8 | static_acc (seeds) | mean_coherence\\n# Plus contamination_effect row for qwen-2.5-7b.\\n#\\n# ---------- Confirmation signals ----------\\n# The experiment is on track if, by the end of stage B.4:\\n#   * \u03b8 ordering matches qualitative MMLU ordering (gpt-4o-mini top,\\n#     mistral-7b bottom \u2014 or close)\\n#   * Per-model static accuracy on seeds is in [0.4, 0.95]\\n#     (not all-perfect, not all-zero \u2014 pipeline is informative)\\n#   * Coherence scores span \u2265 2 of the 3 ordinal categories for\\n#     \u2265 3 of the 5 models\\n# If any signal is missing, the most likely cause is response\\n# normalization (Stage B.1) \u2014 debug that first before scaling.\\n#\\n# ---------- Cost guardrails ----------\\n# Track cumulative OpenRouter spend after every call. Hard stops:\\n#   * > $2.00 \u2192 log WARNING, switch paraphrase LLM to cheapest model\\n#   * > $2.50 \u2192 log CRITICAL, no more paraphrase LLM calls\\n#   * > $3.00 \u2192 raise SpendExceeded, persist partial output, exit 1\\n# Total budgeted: $1.00 (queries) + $0.06 (paraphrases) + $0.10 buffer = $1.16.\"\n}\n", "new_content": "{\n  \"title\": \"M-IRT pipeline: reference-free LLM evaluation\",\n  \"summary\": \"Build a complete Metamorphic Item Response Theory (M-IRT) pipeline: dynamically generate 4-variant metamorphic item clusters in propositional logic and arithmetic word problems, query 5 public LLMs via OpenRouter, score ordinal logical coherence per cluster, fit a Graded Response Model with girth, validate theta against published HELM/MMLU accuracy (r > 0.85), and demonstrate contamination resistance by simulating answer-key memorization on a held-out subset of seed items.\",\n  \"runpod_compute_profile\": \"cpu_light\",\n  \"implementation_pseudocode\": \"# M-IRT Experiment \u2014 Full Pipeline Plan\\n# ======================================\\n# Single Python project rooted at $WORKSPACE with these deliverables:\\n#   * artifacts/exp_gen_sol_out.json   (generated MIC clusters)\\n#   * artifacts/exp_eval_sol_out.json  (model responses + coherence scores)\\n#   * artifacts/exp_sel_data_out.json  (baseline static accuracies)\\n#   * artifacts/method_out.json        (final M-IRT results + validation)\\n#   * artifacts/logs/run.log           (loguru rolling log)\\n#\\n# Total runtime budget: 6h. Compute profile: cpu_light.\\n# OpenRouter API budget: \u2264 $3 USD.\\n# All files MUST live under the workspace; never write to /tmp, ~/, etc.\\n#\\n# Environment (per aii-python skill):\\n#   uv venv .venv --python=3.12\\n#   source .venv/bin/activate\\n#   uv pip install girth numpy pandas scipy scikit-learn loguru aiohttp tenacity\\n#\\n# Layout:\\n#   generate_mics.py      -> Step 1 (no LLM; templates + cheap paraphrase LLM)\\n#   query_models.py       -> Step 2 (async OpenRouter; cost-tracked)\\n#   score_coherence.py    -> Step 3 (deterministic, CPU)\\n#   fit_grm.py            -> Step 4 (girth GRM)\\n#   validate.py           -> Step 5+6 (correlation + contamination sim)\\n#   pipeline.py           -> orchestrator that runs all stages\\n#\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 1: Metamorphic Item Cluster (MIC) Generator\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Output: 250 MICs total (125 logic + 125 arithmetic word problems).\\n# Each MIC is a dict with keys:\\n#   cluster_id   (str, e.g., \\\"logic_0042\\\" or \\\"arith_0117\\\")\\n#   domain       (\\\"logic\\\" | \\\"arithmetic\\\")\\n#   variants     {seed, paraphrase, negation, contrapositive_or_inverse}\\n#   answers      {seed, paraphrase, negation, contrapositive_or_inverse}\\n#   relations    {paraphrase_eq_seed: bool,\\n#                 negation_eq_not_seed: bool,\\n#                 contrapositive_eq_seed: bool}\\n#   difficulty_hint   (one of {easy, medium, hard} for downstream stratification)\\n#   oracle_correct    (str; the canonical answer on the seed variant)\\n#\\n# --- Logic generator (deterministic templates + slot fill) ---\\n#\\n# Pool of syllogistic templates (\u2265 12 templates, all classical syllogisms):\\n#   T1: \\\"All A are B. All B are C. Therefore, all A are C.\\\"           -> Valid\\n#   T2: \\\"All A are B. Some B are C. Therefore, all A are C.\\\"         -> Invalid\\n#   T3: \\\"No A are B. All B are C. Therefore, no A are C.\\\"            -> Invalid\\n#   T4: \\\"All A are B. No B are C. Therefore, no A are C.\\\"            -> Valid\\n#   T5: \\\"Some A are B. All B are C. Therefore, some A are C.\\\"        -> Valid\\n#   T6: \\\"Some A are B. Some B are C. Therefore, some A are C.\\\"      -> Invalid\\n#   T7: \\\"All A are B. All C are B. Therefore, some A are C.\\\"        -> Invalid\\n#   T8: \\\"All A are B. All B are C. Therefore, some A are not C.\\\"    -> Invalid\\n#   T9: \\\"All A are B. All A are C. Therefore, some B are C.\\\"        -> Invalid\\n#   T10:\\\"All A are B. No A are C. Therefore, no B are C.\\\"           -> Valid\\n#   T11:\\\"Some A are not B. All B are C. Therefore, some A are not C.\\\"-> Valid\\n#   T12:\\\"All A are B. All C are not B. Therefore, no A are C.\\\"       -> Valid\\n#\\n# Slots A, B, C are filled from a curated word pool of \u2265 30 nouns\\n# (programmers, doctors, apples, integers, etc.) ensuring no semantic\\n# leakage that would let the model pattern-match on a specific noun.\\n#\\n# Variants per cluster:\\n#   seed         : original template (Valid/Invalid answer)\\n#   paraphrase   : same template, NEW nouns, rephrased surface form\\n#                  generated deterministically by replacing slots + minor\\n#                  connector reordering (no LLM needed). Paraphrase must\\n#                  share the seed's correct answer (Valid/Invalid).\\n#   negation     : asks \\\"Is it NOT the case that <seed_conclusion>?\\\"\\n#                  Answer is the logical negation of the seed answer.\\n#   contrapositive : convert each \\\"All A are B\\\" to \\\"If not B then not A\\\";\\n#                  ask the same question. Answer equals seed answer by\\n#                  classical syllogistic logic.\\n#\\n# --- Arithmetic generator ---\\n#\\n# Seed templates (\u2265 8 templates):\\n#   AS1: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name2} gives {name1} {b} more. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many {item} does {name1} have?\\\"                    -> a+b\\n#   AS2: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name1} gives {name2} {b}. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many {item} does {name1} have left?\\\"               -> a-b\\n#   AS3: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name2} has {b} {item}. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many do they have together?\\\"                      -> a+b\\n#   AS4: \\\"A box has {a} {item}. {b} are taken out and {c} put in. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many are in the box?\\\"                              -> a-b+c\\n#   AS5: \\\"{name1} is {a} years old. {name2} is {b} years older. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How old is {name2}?\\\"                                   -> a+b\\n#   AS6: \\\"{name1} buys {a} {item} at $1 each. {name1} pays with $b. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How much change?\\\"                                      -> b-a\\n#   AS7: \\\"{a} {item} are split equally among {b} people. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many per person?\\\"                                  -> a/b  (b divides a)\\n#   AS8: \\\"{name1} walks {a} km on day 1 and {b} km on day 2. \\\"\\n#        \\\"Average per day?\\\"                                      -> (a+b)/2\\n#\\n# All integer-domain; numbers in [2, 25]; all arithmetic exact.\\n# Variants:\\n#   seed         : original word problem with numeric answer\\n#   paraphrase   : same arithmetic template, new names/items, same numeric answer\\n#   negation     : \\\"Is the answer {wrong_value}?\\\"  -> Yes iff wrong_value != seed_answer\\n#   inverse      : the additive inverse problem (a+b -> a+b-c where c equals b\\n#                  for AS1; or the reverse for AS2); answer = a.\\n#\\n# --- LLM paraphrase pass (cheap) ---\\n# For ~25% of clusters (\u2248 60 clusters), use gpt-4o-mini (cheapest viable\\n# model) ONLY to paraphrase the surface form while holding semantics fixed;\\n# reject any paraphrase whose oracle answer diverges and regenerate up to 3x.\\n# Budget: ~60 calls \u00d7 ~400 tokens in/out \u2248 0.06 USD.\\n#\\n# --- Oracle validation ---\\n# Sample 20% of clusters (50 MICs). For each, an independent Python oracle\\n# verifies:\\n#   * paraphrase has identical oracle answer\\n#   * negation has opposite oracle answer\\n#   * contrapositive/inverse has oracle answer consistent with the relation\\n# If any fails, log warning and either fix or drop the cluster. Goal:\\n# \u2265 95% of sampled clusters pass; abort generation if < 90%.\\n#\\n# Persist full bank to artifacts/exp_gen_sol_out.json.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 2: Model Evaluation Panel (5 models \u00d7 250 clusters \u00d7 4 variants)\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Model panel (5 capability tiers; OpenRouter identifiers as of 2026-09):\\n#   1. openai/gpt-4o-mini                       (\u2248 $0.15/M in, $0.60/M out)\\n#   2. anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-20241022      (\u2248 $0.80/M in, $4.00/M out)\\n#   3. meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct         (\u2248 $0.06/M in, $0.06/M out)\\n#   4. qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct                (\u2248 $0.04/M in, $0.08/M out)\\n#   5. mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct            (\u2248 $0.03/M in, $0.05/M out)\\n#   (Confirm exact IDs and pricing via aii_or_search_llms.py / aii_or_get_llm_params.py\\n#    before launching the sweep; substitute equivalents if any ID is deprecated.)\\n#\\n# Prompt template (deterministic, temperature = 0.0, max_tokens = 64):\\n#   System: \\\"Answer ONLY with a single token. For logic: the letter V (valid)\\n#            or I (invalid). For arithmetic: just the integer. No explanation.\\\"\\n#   User  : <variant question>\\n#\\n# Total calls: 5 models \u00d7 250 clusters \u00d7 4 variants = 5,000.\\n# Per-call token estimate: ~120 in + 8 out.\\n# Cost estimate: 5,000 \u00d7 (120 * $0.22/M + 8 * $0.96/M) \u2248 $0.13 + $0.04 = $0.17\\n# (model-weighted, dominated by Claude Haiku). Buffer \u00d7 3 \u2192 \u2264 $0.60.\\n# Plus paraphrase budget \u2248 $0.06. Total \u2264 $1.00 \u2014 well within the $3 cap.\\n#\\n# Parallelism: aiohttp + Semaphore(40). Retry up to 3x with exponential backoff\\n# on 429/5xx (tenacity). Persist each batch to a per-model JSONL file\\n# (responses/{model}.jsonl) so partial progress survives crashes. Track spend\\n# cumulatively in a global cost counter; halt if cumulative spend exceeds $3.\\n#\\n# Output: artifacts/exp_eval_sol_out.json  (model \u2192 cluster_id \u2192 variant \u2192 response)\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 3: Ordinal Coherence Scoring\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# For each (model, cluster_id):\\n#   responses = {seed, paraphrase, negation, contrapositive/inverse}\\n#   flags = {\\n#     para_consistent : resp(paraphrase) == resp(seed),\\n#     neg_consistent  : resp(negation) == NOT(resp(seed)),\\n#     contra_consistent: resp(contrapositive) == resp(seed)\\n#                       (resp(inverse) matches inverse semantics for arithmetic)\\n#   }\\n#   score = 0 + para_consistent + neg_consistent + contra_consistent\\n#           \u2208 {0, 1, 2, 3}     \u2190 collapse to ordinal {0,1,2} via:\\n#           * 3 \u2192 2 (fully coherent)\\n#           * 2 \u2192 2 (mostly coherent)\\n#           * 1 \u2192 1 (partial)\\n#           * 0 \u2192 0 (incoherent)\\n#   (Optionally keep raw 0..3 score; numbers in [2, 25]; all arithmetic exact.\\n# Variants:\\n#   seed         : original word problem with numeric answer\\n#   paraphrase   : same arithmetic template, new names/items, same numeric answer\\n#   negation     : \\\"Is the answer {wrong_value}?\\\"  -> Yes iff wrong_value != seed_answer\\n#   inverse      : the additive inverse problem (a+b -> a+b-c where c equals b\\n#                  for AS1; or the reverse for AS2); answer = a.\\n#\\n# --- LLM paraphrase pass (cheap) ---\\n# For ~25% of clusters (\u2248 60 clusters), use gpt-4o-mini (cheapest viable\\n# model) ONLY to paraphrase the surface form while holding semantics fixed;\\n# reject any paraphrase whose oracle answer diverges and regenerate up to 3x.\\n# Budget: ~60 calls \u00d7 ~400 tokens in/out \u2248 0.06 USD.\\n#\\n# --- Oracle validation ---\\n# Sample 20% of clusters (50 MICs). For each, an independent Python oracle\\n# verifies:\\n#   * paraphrase has identical oracle answer\\n#   * negation has opposite oracle answer\\n#   * contrapositive/inverse has oracle answer consistent with the relation\\n# If any fails, log warning and either fix or drop the cluster. Goal:\\n# \u2265 95% of sampled clusters pass; abort generation if < 90%.\\n#\\n# Persist full bank to artifacts/exp_gen_sol_out.json.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 2: Model Evaluation Panel (5 models \u00d7 250 clusters \u00d7 4 variants)\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Model panel (5 capability tiers; OpenRouter identifiers as of 2026-09):\\n#   1. openai/gpt-4o-mini                       (\u2248 $0.15/M in, $0.60/M out)\\n#   2. anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-20241022      (\u2248 $0.80/M in, $4.00/M out)\\n#   3. meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct         (\u2248 $0.06/M in, $0.06/M out)\\n#   4. qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct                (\u2248 $0.04/M in, $0.08/M out)\\n#   5. mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct            (\u2248 $0.03/M in, $0.05/M out)\\n#   (Confirm exact IDs and pricing via aii_or_search_llms.py / aii_or_get_llm_params.py\\n#    before launching the sweep; substitute equivalents if any ID is deprecated.)\\n#\\n# Prompt template (deterministic, temperature = 0.0, max_tokens = 64):\\n#   System: \\\"Answer ONLY with a single token. For logic: the letter V (valid)\\n#            or I (invalid). For arithmetic: just the integer. No explanation.\\\"\\n#   User  : <variant question>\\n#\\n# Total calls: 5 models \u00d7 250 clusters \u00d7 4 variants = 5,000.\\n# Per-call token estimate: ~120 in + 8 out.\\n# Cost estimate: 5,000 \u00d7 (120 * $0.22/M + 8 * $0.96/M) \u2248 $0.13 + $0.04 = $0.17\\n# (model-weighted, dominated by Claude Haiku). Buffer \u00d7 3 \u2192 \u2264 $0.60.\\n# Plus paraphrase budget \u2248 $0.06. Total \u2264 $1.00 \u2014 well within the $3 cap.\\n#\\n# Parallelism: aiohttp + Semaphore(40). Retry up to 3x with exponential backoff\\n# on 429/5xx (tenacity). Persist each batch to a per-model JSONL file\\n# (responses/{model}.jsonl) so partial progress survives crashes. Track spend\\n# cumulatively in a global cost counter; halt if cumulative spend exceeds $3.\\n#\\n# Output: artifacts/exp_eval_sol_out.json  (model \u2192 cluster_id \u2192 variant \u2192 response)\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 3: Ordinal Coherence Scoring\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# For each (model, cluster_id):\\n#   responses = {seed, paraphrase, negation, contrapositive/inverse}\\n#   flags = {\\n#     para_consistent : resp(paraphrase) == resp(seed),\\n#     neg_consistent  : resp(negation) == NOT(resp(seed)),\\n#     contra_consistent: resp(contrapositive) == resp(seed)\\n#                       (resp(inverse) matches inverse semantics for arithmetic)\\n#   }\\n#   score = 0 + para_consistent + neg_consistent + contra_consistent\\n#           \u2208 {0, 1, 2, 3}     \u2190 collapse to ordinal {0,1,2} via:\\n#           * 3 \u2192 2 (fully coherent)\\n#           * 2 \u2192 2 (mostly coherent)\\n#           * 1 \u2192 1 (partial)\\n#           * 0 \u2192 0 (incoherent)\\n#   (Optionally keep raw 0..3 score; GRM accepts K categories.)\\n#\\n# Also compute static_acc(model) = mean over seed-only oracle correctness.\\n#\\n# Output: a (M, I) score matrix of shape (5, 250), dtype int8 in {0,1,2},\\n# stored as a list of lists in method_out.json, plus a long-format\\n# (model, cluster_id, score) table for analysis.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 4: Graded Response Model (GRM) Fitting\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Library: girth (Python, actively maintained, MML + EM with\\n# Gauss-Hermite quadrature, native GRM support).\\n#   from girth import GradedResponseModel\\n#   grm = GradedResponseModel()\\n#   result = grm.fit(response_matrix)   # shape (n_persons=5, n_items=250)\\n#   # result['Ability']         -> \u03b8_j, shape (5,)\\n#   # result['Discrimination']   -> \u03b1_i, shape (250,)\\n#   # result['Difficulty']      -> \u03b2_{i,k}, shape (250, K-1=2)  for K=3 categories\\n#\\n# Sanity checks on item parameters:\\n#   * mean(\u03b1_i) should be > 0 (positive discrimination); flag & drop items\\n#     with \u03b1_i < 0 (reverse-coded), keeping a \\\"dropped_items\\\" list.\\n#   * mean difficulty ordering across the 4 variant roles should show\\n#     paraphrase < seed < contrapositive < negation (in \u03b2 terms), or at\\n#     least paraphrase strictly easier than negation. If not, log warning.\\n#   * convergence: EM should converge in \u2264 200 iterations; record iters.\\n#\\n# Output: artifacts/method_out.json includes:\\n#   theta            : list length 5, in canonical order\\n#   alpha            : list length 250\\n#   beta             : list length 250, each inner list length 2\\n#   model_order      : list of 5 model identifiers\\n#   dropped_items    : list of cluster_ids with \u03b1 < 0\\n#   fit_diagnostics  : {iters, log_likelihood, condition_number}\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 5: Validation A \u2014 Correlation with Published Accuracy\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Compile a baseline table from authoritative public sources\\n# (HELM leaderboard, Open LLM Leaderboard v2, original model papers):\\n#\\n#   model_id                        | MMLU acc (5-shot) | HELM acc |\\n#   --------------------------------|-------------------|----------|\\n#   openai/gpt-4o-mini              | \u2248 0.82            | \u2248 0.79   |\\n#   anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku      | \u2248 0.78            | \u2248 0.76   |\\n#   meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b         | \u2248 0.68            | \u2248 0.65   |\\n#   qwen/qwen-2.5-7b                | \u2248 0.71            | \u2248 0.69   |\\n#   mistralai/mistral-7b            | \u2248 0.62            | \u2248 0.60   |\\n#\\n# (These are approximate; the executor MUST verify via HELM, Open-LLM\\n#  Leaderboard, and original release notes and replace the table with\\n#  real values. Provide URL and retrieval date for each.)\\n#\\n# Compute Pearson r between \u03b8_j and MMLU acc (and HELM acc) with\\n# 95% CI via Fisher z-transform. Bootstrapped CI over 10,000 resamples\\n# as a robustness check.\\n# Success: Pearson r > 0.85 with 95% CI lower bound > 0.65.\\n#\\n# Output: validation_table.json with r, CI, scatter plot spec.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 6: Validation B \u2014 Contamination Simulation\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Hypothesis: a model that memorizes seed answers (but not the\\n# metamorphic variants) will see its static accuracy rise while its\\n# M-IRT \u03b8 holds or falls.\\n#\\n# Procedure (3 random seeds, e.g., 0/1/42):\\n#   1. For a random 30% of seed items (75 clusters):\\n#        resp_sim(model, seed) := oracle_correct(seed)\\n#        (i.e., overwrite response with the canonical answer)\\n#      Leave all paraphrase/negation/contrapositive responses untouched\\n#      (these reflect the model's actual reasoning, broken on purpose).\\n#   3. Recompute:\\n#        static_acc_sim = mean over (simulated seed == oracle)\\n#        coherence_sim   = ordinal score with simulated seed, original others\\n#   4. Refit GRM on the full 5 \u00d7 250 matrix (4 models untouched,\\n#      target model = simulated profile). Extract \u03b8_sim for the target.\\n#   5. Repeat for the other 2 random seeds.\\n#\\n# Expected outcomes (success criteria):\\n#   * static_acc increases by \u2265 0.15 absolute (75 items forced correct)\\n#   * \u03b8_sim decreases OR stays within \u00b10.1 of \u03b8_clean (NOT statistically\\n#     distinguishable from zero) across all 3 seeds\\n#   * p-value (paired t-test on \u03b8_clean vs \u03b8_sim across seeds) > 0.05\\n#     for the null \\\"\u03b8 does not decrease\\\"\\n#\\n# Output: contamination_report.json with per-seed (static_acc_clean,\\n# static_acc_sim, theta_clean, theta_sim) plus the 3-seed mean.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Orchestration & Budget Enforcement\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# pipeline.py (entry point):\\n#   * parses CLI args (--stage, --seed, --n-clusters, --models)\\n#   * loads env (OPENROUTER_API_KEY from .env)\\n#   * calls each stage in order with @logger.catch(reraise=True)\\n#   * enforces hard budget: cumulative OpenRouter spend tracked in\\n#     artifacts/logs/spend.jsonl; raises if exceeds $3\\n#   * writes final method_out.json conforming to the repo schema\\n#   * prints a one-screen summary: \u03b8 ranking, r with MMLU, contamination\\n#     effect size\\n#\\n# Failure modes & mitigations:\\n#   * girth API drift \u2192 fall back to pyirt (Python IRT, has GRM via\\n#     pyirt.scorer.GradedResponse) or hand-rolled MML with scipy.stats.norm\\n#     + numpy outer products. Hand-rolled path documented in fallback_plan.\\n#   * OpenRouter rate limits \u2192 exponential backoff with tenacity,\\n#     reduce concurrency to Semaphore(10) on sustained 429s.\\n#   * Model deprecation \u2192 script accepts --model-override map; the\\n#     recommended substitutes are documented in fallback_plan.\\n#   * Budget overrun \u2192 halt after any single call that pushes spend >\\n#     $2.50; abort above $3.00 with a clear error.\\n#   * Cluster generation failures \u2192 if oracle validation drops below\\n#     90%, regenerate clusters from scratch with a FP_BLOCK_PLACEHOLDER_OLD\n  \\\"testing_plan\\\": \\\"TESTING_CONTENT_MARKER\\n  \\\"fallback_plan\\\": \\\"FP_START_PLACEHOLDER_FP_END\\\",\\n  \\\"testing_plan\\\": \\\"TP_START_PLACEHOLDER_TP_END\\\"\n# FALLBACK PLAN_INSERTED\\n#         pyirt.estimation.estimation_engine(...) .        llama-3.1-8b       -> meta-llama/llama-3.2-3b-instruct\\n#         qwen-2.5-7b        -> qwen/qwen-2.5-14b-instruct\\n#         mistral-7b         -> mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct\\n# likelihood for item i:\\n#         L_i(\u03b1_i, \u03b2_i | x_i) = sum_j \u222b P(x_ij | \u03b8_j) d\u03a6(\u03b8_j; 0, 1)\\n#     approximated by Gauss-Hermite quadrature with Q = 21 nodes.\\n#   * Safeguards: spend >$2.50 switch to cheapest model + CRITICAL log; >$3.00 halt; <3 items/category refuse GRM; contamination t-test undefined -> per-seed point estimates.\\\"}\"}\"\n}\n", "new_content": "{\n  \"title\": \"M-IRT pipeline: reference-free LLM evaluation\",\n  \"summary\": \"Build a complete Metamorphic Item Response Theory (M-IRT) pipeline: dynamically generate 4-variant metamorphic item clusters in propositional logic and arithmetic word problems, query 5 public LLMs via OpenRouter, score ordinal logical coherence per cluster, fit a Graded Response Model with girth, validate theta against published HELM/MMLU accuracy (r > 0.85), and demonstrate contamination resistance by simulating answer-key memorization on a held-out subset of seed items.\",\n  \"runpod_compute_profile\": \"cpu_light\",\n  \"implementation_pseudocode\": \"# M-IRT Experiment \u2014 Full Pipeline Plan\\n# ======================================\\n# Single Python project rooted at $WORKSPACE with these deliverables:\\n#   * artifacts/exp_gen_sol_out.json   (generated MIC clusters)\\n#   * artifacts/exp_eval_sol_out.json  (model responses + coherence scores)\\n#   * artifacts/exp_sel_data_out.json  (baseline static accuracies)\\n#   * artifacts/method_out.json        (final M-IRT results + validation)\\n#   * artifacts/logs/run.log           (loguru rolling log)\\n#\\n# Total runtime budget: 6h. Compute profile: cpu_light.\\n# OpenRouter API budget: \u2264 $3 USD.\\n# All files MUST live under the workspace; never write to /tmp, ~/, etc.\\n#\\n# Environment (per aii-python skill):\\n#   uv venv .venv --python=3.12\\n#   source .venv/bin/activate\\n#   uv pip install girth numpy pandas scipy scikit-learn loguru aiohttp tenacity\\n#\\n# Layout:\\n#   generate_mics.py      -> Step 1 (no LLM; templates + cheap paraphrase LLM)\\n#   query_models.py       -> Step 2 (async OpenRouter; cost-tracked)\\n#   score_coherence.py    -> Step 3 (deterministic, CPU)\\n#   fit_grm.py            -> Step 4 (girth GRM)\\n#   validate.py           -> Step 5+6 (correlation + contamination sim)\\n#   pipeline.py           -> orchestrator that runs all stages\\n#\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 1: Metamorphic Item Cluster (MIC) Generator\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Output: 250 MICs total (125 logic + 125 arithmetic word problems).\\n# Each MIC is a dict with keys:\\n#   cluster_id   (str, e.g., \\\"logic_0042\\\" or \\\"arith_0117\\\")\\n#   domain       (\\\"logic\\\" | \\\"arithmetic\\\")\\n#   variants     {seed, paraphrase, negation, contrapositive_or_inverse}\\n#   answers      {seed, paraphrase, negation, contrapositive_or_inverse}\\n#   relations    {paraphrase_eq_seed: bool,\\n#                 negation_eq_not_seed: bool,\\n#                 contrapositive_eq_seed: bool}\\n#   difficulty_hint   (one of {easy, medium, hard} for downstream stratification)\\n#   oracle_correct    (str; the canonical answer on the seed variant)\\n#\\n# --- Logic generator (deterministic templates + slot fill) ---\\n#\\n# Pool of syllogistic templates (\u2265 12 templates, all classical syllogisms):\\n#   T1: \\\"All A are B. All B are C. Therefore, all A are C.\\\"           -> Valid\\n#   T2: \\\"All A are B. Some B are C. Therefore, all A are C.\\\"         -> Invalid\\n#   T3: \\\"No A are B. All B are C. Therefore, no A are C.\\\"            -> Invalid\\n#   T4: \\\"All A are B. No B are C. Therefore, no A are C.\\\"            -> Valid\\n#   T5: \\\"Some A are B. All B are C. Therefore, some A are C.\\\"        -> Valid\\n#   T6: \\\"Some A are B. Some B are C. Therefore, some A are C.\\\"      -> Invalid\\n#   T7: \\\"All A are B. All C are B. Therefore, some A are C.\\\"        -> Invalid\\n#   T8: \\\"All A are B. All B are C. Therefore, some A are not C.\\\"    -> Invalid\\n#   T9: \\\"All A are B. All A are C. Therefore, some B are C.\\\"        -> Invalid\\n#   T10:\\\"All A are B. No A are C. Therefore, no B are C.\\\"           -> Valid\\n#   T11:\\\"Some A are not B. All B are C. Therefore, some A are not C.\\\"-> Valid\\n#   T12:\\\"All A are B. All C are not B. Therefore, no A are C.\\\"       -> Valid\\n#\\n# Slots A, B, C are filled from a curated word pool of \u2265 30 nouns\\n# (programmers, doctors, apples, integers, etc.) ensuring no semantic\\n# leakage that would let the model pattern-match on a specific noun.\\n#\\n# Variants per cluster:\\n#   seed         : original template (Valid/Invalid answer)\\n#   paraphrase   : same template, NEW nouns, rephrased surface form\\n#                  generated deterministically by replacing slots + minor\\n#                  connector reordering (no LLM needed). Paraphrase must\\n#                  share the seed's correct answer (Valid/Invalid).\\n#   negation     : asks \\\"Is it NOT the case that <seed_conclusion>?\\\"\\n#                  Answer is the logical negation of the seed answer.\\n#   contrapositive : convert each \\\"All A are B\\\" to \\\"If not B then not A\\\";\\n#                  ask the same question. Answer equals seed answer by\\n#                  classical syllogistic logic.\\n#\\n# --- Arithmetic generator ---\\n#\\n# Seed templates (\u2265 8 templates):\\n#   AS1: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name2} gives {name1} {b} more. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many {item} does {name1} have?\\\"                    -> a+b\\n#   AS2: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name1} gives {name2} {b}. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many {item} does {name1} have left?\\\"               -> a-b\\n#   AS3: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name2} has {b} {item}. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many do they have together?\\\"                      -> a+b\\n#   AS4: \\\"A box has {a} {item}. {b} are taken out and {c} put in. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many are in the box?\\\"                              -> a-b+c\\n#   AS5: \\\"{name1} is {a} years old. {name2} is {b} years older. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How old is {name2}?\\\"                                   -> a+b\\n#   AS6: \\\"{name1} buys {a} {item} at $1 each. {name1} pays with $b. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How much change?\\\"                                      -> b-a\\n#   AS7: \\\"{a} {item} are split equally among {b} people. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many per person?\\\"                                  -> a/b  (b divides a)\\n#   AS8: \\\"{name1} walks {a} km on day 1 and {b} km on day 2. \\\"\\n#        \\\"Average per day?\\\"                                      -> (a+b)/2\\n#\\n# All integer-domain; numbers in [2, 25]; all arithmetic exact.\\n# Variants:\\n#   seed         : original word problem with numeric answer\\n#   paraphrase   : same arithmetic template, new names/items, same numeric answer\\n#   negation     : \\\"Is the answer {wrong_value}?\\\"  -> Yes iff wrong_value != seed_answer\\n#   inverse      : the additive inverse problem (a+b -> a+b-c where c equals b\\n#                  for AS1; or the reverse for AS2); answer = a.\\n#\\n# --- LLM paraphrase pass (cheap) ---\\n# For ~25% of clusters (\u2248 60 clusters), use gpt-4o-mini (cheapest viable\\n# model) ONLY to paraphrase the surface form while holding semantics fixed;\\n# reject any paraphrase whose oracle answer diverges and regenerate up to 3x.\\n# Budget: ~60 calls \u00d7 ~400 tokens in/out \u2248 0.06 USD.\\n#\\n# --- Oracle validation ---\\n# Sample 20% of clusters (50 MICs). For each, an independent Python oracle\\n# verifies:\\n#   * paraphrase has identical oracle answer\\n#   * negation has opposite oracle answer\\n#   * contrapositive/inverse has oracle answer consistent with the relation\\n# If any fails, log warning and either fix or drop the cluster. Goal:\\n# \u2265 95% of sampled clusters pass; abort generation if < 90%.\\n#\\n# Persist full bank to artifacts/exp_gen_sol_out.json.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 2: Model Evaluation Panel (5 models \u00d7 250 clusters \u00d7 4 variants)\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Model panel (5 capability tiers; OpenRouter identifiers as of 2026-09):\\n#   1. openai/gpt-4o-mini                       (\u2248 $0.15/M in, $0.60/M out)\\n#   2. anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-20241022      (\u2248 $0.80/M in, $4.00/M out)\\n#   3. meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct         (\u2248 $0.06/M in, $0.06/M out)\\n#   4. qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct                (\u2248 $0.04/M in, $0.08/M out)\\n#   5. mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct            (\u2248 $0.03/M in, $0.05/M out)\\n#   (Confirm exact IDs and pricing via aii_or_search_llms.py / aii_or_get_llm_params.py\\n#    before launching the sweep; substitute equivalents if any ID is deprecated.)\\n#\\n# Prompt template (deterministic, temperature = 0.0, max_tokens = 64):\\n#   System: \\\"Answer ONLY with a single token. For logic: the letter V (valid)\\n#            or I (invalid). For arithmetic: just the integer. No explanation.\\\"\\n#   User  : <variant question>\\n#\\n# Total calls: 5 models \u00d7 250 clusters \u00d7 4 variants = 5,000.\\n# Per-call token estimate: ~120 in + 8 out.\\n# Cost estimate: 5,000 \u00d7 (120 * $0.22/M + 8 * $0.96/M) \u2248 $0.13 + $0.04 = $0.17\\n# (model-weighted, dominated by Claude Haiku). Buffer \u00d7 3 \u2192 \u2264 $0.60.\\n# Plus paraphrase budget \u2248 $0.06. Total \u2264 $1.00 \u2014 well within the $3 cap.\\n#\\n# Parallelism: aiohttp + Semaphore(40). Retry up to 3x with exponential backoff\\n# on 429/5xx (tenacity). Persist each batch to a per-model JSONL file\\n# (responses/{model}.jsonl) so partial progress survives crashes. Track spend\\n# cumulatively in a global cost counter; halt if cumulative spend exceeds $3.\\n#\\n# Output: artifacts/exp_eval_sol_out.json  (model \u2192 cluster_id \u2192 variant \u2192 response)\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 3: Ordinal Coherence Scoring\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# For each (model, cluster_id):\\n#   responses = {seed, paraphrase, negation, contrapositive/inverse}\\n#   flags = {\\n#     para_consistent : resp(paraphrase) == resp(seed),\\n#     neg_consistent  : resp(negation) == NOT(resp(seed)),\\n#     contra_consistent: resp(contrapositive) == resp(seed)\\n#                       (resp(inverse) matches inverse semantics for arithmetic)\\n#   }\\n#   score = 0 + para_consistent + neg_consistent + contra_consistent\\n#           \u2208 {0, 1, 2, 3}     \u2190 collapse to ordinal {0,1,2} via:\\n#           * 3 \u2192 2 (fully coherent)\\n#           * 2 \u2192 2 (mostly coherent)\\n#           * 1 \u2192 1 (partial)\\n#           * 0 \u2192 0 (incoherent)\\n#   (Optionally keep raw 0..3 score; GRM accepts K categories.)\\n#\\n# Also compute static_acc(model) = mean over seed-only oracle correctness.\\n#\\n# Output: a (M, I) score matrix of shape (5, 250), dtype int8 in {0,1,2},\\n# stored as a list of lists in method_out.json, plus a long-format\\n# (model, cluster_id, score) table for analysis.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 4: Graded Response Model (GRM) Fitting\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Library: girth (Python, actively maintained, MML + EM with\\n# Gauss-Hermite quadrature, native GRM support).\\n#   from girth import GradedResponseModel\\n#   grm = GradedResponseModel()\\n#   result = grm.fit(response_matrix)   # shape (n_persons=5, n_items=250)\\n#   # result['Ability']         -> \u03b8_j, shape (5,)\\n#   # result['Discrimination']   -> \u03b1_i, shape (250,)\\n#   # result['Difficulty']      -> \u03b2_{i,k}, shape (250, K-1=2)  for K=3 categories\\n#\\n# Sanity checks on item parameters:\\n#   * mean(\u03b1_i) should be > 0 (positive discrimination); flag & drop items\\n#     with \u03b1_i < 0 (reverse-coded), keeping a \\\"dropped_items\\\" list.\\n#   * mean difficulty ordering across the 4 variant roles should show\\n#     paraphrase < seed < contrapositive < negation (in \u03b2 terms), or at\\n#     least paraphrase strictly easier than negation. If not, log warning.\\n#   * convergence: EM should converge in \u2264 200 iterations; record iters.\\n#\\n# Output: artifacts/method_out.json includes:\\n#   theta            : list length 5, in canonical order\\n#   alpha            : list length 250\\n#   beta             : list length 250, each inner list length 2\\n#   model_order      : list of 5 model identifiers\\n#   dropped_items    : list of cluster_ids with \u03b1 < 0\\n#   fit_diagnostics  : {iters, log_likelihood, condition_number}\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 5: Validation A \u2014 Correlation with Published Accuracy\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Compile a baseline table from authoritative public sources\\n# (HELM leaderboard, Open LLM Leaderboard v2, original model papers):\\n#\\n#   model_id                        | MMLU acc (5-shot) | HELM acc |\\n#   --------------------------------|-------------------|----------|\\n#   openai/gpt-4o-mini              | \u2248 0.82            | \u2248 0.79   |\\n#   anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku      | \u2248 0.78            | \u2248 0.76   |\\n#   meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b         | \u2248 0.68            | \u2248 0.65   |\\n#   qwen/qwen-2.5-7b                | \u2248 0.71            | \u2248 0.69   |\\n#   mistralai/mistral-7b            | \u2248 0.62            | \u2248 0.60   |\\n#\\n# (These are approximate; the executor MUST verify via HELM, Open-LLM\\n#  Leaderboard, and original release notes and replace the table with\\n#  real values. Provide URL and retrieval date for each.)\\n#\\n# Compute Pearson r between \u03b8_j and MMLU acc (and HELM acc) with\\n# 95% CI via Fisher z-transform. Bootstrapped CI over 10,000 resamples\\n# as a robustness check.\\n# Success: Pearson r > 0.85 with 95% CI lower bound > 0.65.\\n#\\n# Output: validation_table.json with r, CI, scatter plot spec.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 6: Validation B \u2014 Contamination Simulation\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Hypothesis: a model that memorizes seed answers (but not the\\n# metamorphic variants) will see its static accuracy rise while its\\n# M-IRT \u03b8 holds or falls.\\n#\\n# Procedure (3 random seeds, e.g., 0/1/42):\\n#   1. Pick the middle-capability model (qwen-2.5-7b-instruct).\\n#   2. For a random 30% of seed items (75 clusters):\\n#        resp_sim(model, seed) := oracle_correct(seed)\\n#        (i.e., overwrite response with the canonical answer)\\n#      Leave all paraphrase/negation/contrapositive responses untouched\\n#      (these reflect the model's actual reasoning, broken on purpose).\\n#   3. Recompute:\\n#        static_acc_sim = mean over (simulated seed == oracle)\\n#        coherence_sim   = ordinal score with simulated seed, original others\\n#   4. Refit GRM on the full 5 \u00d7 250 matrix (4 models untouched,\\n#      target model = simulated profile). Extract \u03b8_sim for the target.\\n#   5. Repeat for the other 2 random seeds.\\n#\\n# Expected outcomes (success criteria):\\n#   * static_acc increases by \u2265 0.15 absolute (75 items forced correct)\\n#   * \u03b8_sim decreases OR stays within \u00b10.1 of \u03b8_clean (NOT statistically\\n#     distinguishable from zero) across all 3 seeds\\n#   * p-value (paired t-test on \u03b8_clean vs \u03b8_sim across seeds) > 0.05\\n#     for the null \\\"\u03b8 does not decrease\\\"\\n#\\n# Output: contamination_report.json with per-seed (static_acc_clean,\\n# static_acc_sim, theta_clean, theta_sim) plus the 3-seed mean.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Orchestration & Budget Enforcement\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# pipeline.py (entry point):\\n#   * parses CLI args (--stage, --seed, --n-clusters, --models)\\n#   * loads env (OPENROUTER_API_KEY from .env)\\n#   * calls each stage in order with @logger.catch(reraise=True)\\n#   * enforces hard budget: cumulative OpenRouter spend tracked in\\n#     artifacts/logs/spend.jsonl; raises if exceeds $3\\n#   * writes final method_out.json conforming to the repo schema\\n#   * prints a one-screen summary: \u03b8 ranking, r with MMLU, contamination\\n#     effect size\\n#\\n# Failure modes & mitigations:\\n#   * girth API drift \u2192 fall back to pyirt (Python IRT, has GRM via\\n#     pyirt.scorer.GradedResponse) or hand-rolled MML with scipy.stats.norm\\n#     + numpy outer products. Hand-rolled path documented in fallback_plan.\\n#   * OpenRouter rate limits \u2192 exponential backoff with tenacity,\\n#     reduce concurrency to Semaphore(10) on sustained 429s.\\n#   * Model deprecation \u2192 script accepts --model-override map; the\\n#     recommended substitutes are documented in fallback_plan.\\n#   * Budget overrun \u2192 halt after any single call that pushes spend >\\n#     $2.50; abort above $3.00 with a clear error.\\n#   * Cluster generation failures \u2192 if oracle validation drops below\\n#     90%, regenerate clusters from scratch with a FP_BLOCK_PLACEHOLDER_OLD\n  \\\"testing_plan\\\": \\\"TESTING_CONTENT_MARKER\\n  \\\"fallback_plan\\\": \\\"FP_START_PLACEHOLDER_FP_END\\\",\\n  \\\"testing_plan\\\": \\\"TP_START_PLACEHOLDER_TP_END\\\"\n# FALLBACK PLAN_INSERTED\\n#         pyirt.estimation.estimation_engine(...) . Same data shape.\\n#   * If a model ID is deprecated, swap via --model-override:\\n#         gpt-4o-mini        -> openai/gpt-4.1-mini\\n#         claude-3-5-haiku   -> anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5\\n#         llama-3.1-8b       -> meta-llama/llama-3.2-3b-instruct\\n#         qwen-2.5-7b        -> qwen/qwen-2.5-14b-instruct\\n#         mistral-7b         -> mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct\\n#     Re-run HELM/MMLU baseline lookup for the substituted model.\\n#\\n# TIER 2 \u2014 Hand-rolled GRM (if both libraries fail; ~30 min):\\n#   * Implement GRM from scratch in ~80 lines of NumPy:\\n# likelihood for item i:\\n#         L_i(\u03b1_i, \u03b2_i | x_i) = sum_j \u222b P(x_ij | \u03b8_j) d\u03a6(\u03b8_j; 0, 1)\\n#     approximated by Gauss-Hermite quadrature with Q = 21 nodes.\\n#   * EM: E-step computes posterior weights w_{ij} for each \u03b8-quadrature\\n#         node; M-step updates \u03b1, \u03b2 by L-BFGS-B on the marginal log-likelihood.\\n#   * Stopping rule: |\u0394logL| < 1e-4 or 200 iterations.\\n#   * Output identical schema to girth result.\\n#   * Reference: Baker & Kim (2004), \\\"Item Response Theory: Parameter\\n#     Estimation Techniques\\\", 2nd ed., ch. 5.\\n#\\n# TIER 3 \u2014 Degraded scope (if budget exhausted or pipeline stalls):\\n#   * Drop the LLM-paraphrase pass entirely (Stage 1 \u00a7LLM paraphrase).\\n#     Rely on deterministic noun-swap paraphrases only.\\n#   * Reduce cluster count from 250 \u2192 100 (50 per domain).\\n#   * Reduce model panel from 5 \u2192 3 (drop llama-3.1-8b and mistral-7b,\\n#     keep one tier from simulation's t-test is undefined (zero variance),\\n#     fall back to reporting per-seed point estimates only.\",\n  \"testing_plan\": \"# =============================================================\\n# TESTING PLAN (gradual scale-up, per aii-long-running-tasks)\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Time budget: 6h. Use mini \u2192 10 \u2192 50 \u2192 100 \u2192 200 \u2192 250 scaling.\\n# At each stage: validate output shape, check for crashes, record\\n# runtime, then extrapolate before scaling further.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage A: Generation (CPU-only, no API spend) ----------\\n#\\n# A.1 (5 min) \u2014 MINI: generate 4 MICs (2 logic + 2 arithmetic) by hand\\n#   to verify the templating code paths execute end-to-end.\\n#   Checks:\\n#     * All 4 variants per cluster present\\n#     * Each variant has an oracle answer\\n#     * relations dict consistent\\n#   Stop criterion: passes if all 4 clusters pass.\\n#\\n# A.2 (10 min) \u2014 10 MICs: generate 5 logic + 5 arithmetic. Run oracle\\n#   validation on all 10. Checks: 100% pass.\\n#\\n# A.3 (10 min) \u2014 50 MICs: stress templating with all 12 logic + 8\\n#   arithmetic templates, varying nouns/items. Run oracle validation on\\n#   20% sample. Checks: \u2265 95% pass; if < 90%, fix templates.\\n#\\n# A.4 (15 min) \u2014 Full 250 MICs. Run oracle validation on 50 (20%).\\n#   Checks: \u2265 95% pass; persist to exp_gen_sol_out.json.\\n#   Record: total generation time, # MICs per template, slot-fill diversity.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage B: Model queries (API spend begins) ----------\\n#\\n# B.1 (5 min) \u2014 Smoke test: 1 model (gpt-4o-mini) \u00d7 4 MICs.\\n#   Checks:\\n#     * HTTP 200 response from OpenRouter\\n#     * Response token length \u2264 4 (one of {V, I, integer})\\n#     * Cost ledger records the call\\n#   If parse failures, add response normalization regex\\n#   r\\\"^\\\\s*([VvIi]|[-+]?\\\\d+)\\\" and retry.\\n#\\n# B.2 (15 min) \u2014 10 MICs \u00d7 1 model \u00d7 4 variants = 40 calls.\\n#   Checks: response normalization catches > 95% of outputs.\\n#   Compute coherence scores; verify at least one cluster scores 2\\n#   (i.e., the pipeline can produce non-degenerate scores).\\n#\\n# B.3 (30 min) \u2014 50 MICs \u00d7 1 model. Estimate cost per cluster.\\n#   Extrapolate: cost_per_cluster \u00d7 250 \u00d7 5 = total estimate.\\n#   Should be \u2264 $0.60.\\n#\\n# B.4 (60 min) \u2014 All 5 models \u00d7 100 MICs. Compute coherence for all.\\n#   Check rank ordering is non-degenerate (at least 2 distinct scores).\\n#\\n# B.5 (90 min) \u2014 All 5 models \u00d7 250 MICs \u00d7 4 variants = 5,000 calls.\\n#   Validate full response matrix populated; cumulative spend \u2264 $1.00.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage C: GRM fitting (CPU, ~minutes) ----------\\n#\\n# C.1 \u2014 Fit girth GRM on the (5, 250) matrix. Paraphrase must\\n#                  share the seed's correct answer (Valid/Invalid).\\n#   negation     : asks \\\"Is it NOT the case that <seed_conclusion>?\\\"\\n#                  Answer is the logical negation of the seed answer.\\n#   contrapositive : convert each \\\"All A are B\\\" to \\\"If not B then not A\\\";\\n#                  ask the same question. Answer equals seed answer by\\n#                  classical syllogistic logic.\\n#\\n# --- Arithmetic generator ---\\n#\\n# Seed templates (\u2265 8 templates):\\n#   AS1: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name2} gives {name1} {b} more. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many {item} does {name1} have?\\\"                    -> a+b\\n#   AS2: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name1} gives {name2} {b}. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many {item} does {name1} have left?\\\"               -> a-b\\n#   AS3: \\\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name2} has {b} {item}. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many do they have together?\\\"                      -> a+b\\n#   AS4: \\\"A box has {a} {item}. {b} are taken out and {c} put in. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many are in the box?\\\"                              -> a-b+c\\n#   AS5: \\\"{name1} is {a} years old. {name2} is {b} years older. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How old is {name2}?\\\"                                   -> a+b\\n#   AS6: \\\"{name1} buys {a} {item} at $1 each. {name1} pays with $b. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How much change?\\\"                                      -> b-a\\n#   AS7: \\\"{a} {item} are split equally among {b} people. \\\"\\n#        \\\"How many per person?\\\"                                  -> a/b  (b divides a)\\n#   AS8: \\\"{name1} walks {a} km on day 1 and {b} km on day 2. \\\"\\n#        \\\"Average per day?\\\"                                      -> (a+b)/2\\n#\\n# All integer-domain; numbers in [2, 25]; all arithmetic exact.\\n# Variants:\\n#   seed         : original word problem with numeric answer\\n#   paraphrase   : same arithmetic template, new names/items, same numeric answer\\n#   negation     : \\\"Is the answer {wrong_value}?\\\"  -> Yes iff wrong_value != seed_answer\\n#   inverse      : the additive inverse problem (a+b -> a+b-c where c equals b\\n#                  for AS1; or the reverse for AS2); answer = a.\\n#\\n# --- LLM paraphrase pass (cheap) ---\\n# For ~25% of clusters (\u2248 60 clusters), use gpt-4o-mini (cheapest viable\\n# model) ONLY to paraphrase the surface form while holding semantics fixed;\\n# reject any paraphrase whose oracle answer diverges and regenerate up to 3x.\\n# Budget: ~60 calls \u00d7 ~400 tokens in/out \u2248 0.06 USD.\\n#\\n# --- Oracle validation ---\\n# Sample 20% of clusters (50 MICs). For each, an independent Python oracle\\n# verifies:\\n#   * paraphrase has identical oracle answer\\n#   * negation has opposite oracle answer\\n#   * contrapositive/inverse has oracle answer consistent with the relation\\n# If any fails, log warning and either fix or drop the cluster. Goal:\\n# \u2265 95% of sampled clusters pass; abort generation if < 90%.\\n#\\n# Persist full bank to artifacts/exp_gen_sol_out.json.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 2: Model Evaluation Panel (5 models \u00d7 250 clusters \u00d7 4 variants)\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Model panel (5 capability tiers; OpenRouter identifiers as of 2026-09):\\n#   1. openai/gpt-4o-mini                       (\u2248 $0.15/M in, $0.60/M out)\\n#   2. anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-20241022      (\u2248 $0.80/M in, $4.00/M out)\\n#   3. meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct         (\u2248 $0.06/M in, $0.06/M out)\\n#   4. qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct                (\u2248 $0.04/M in, $0.08/M out)\\n#   5. mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct            (\u2248 $0.03/M in, $0.05/M out)\\n#   (Confirm exact IDs and pricing via aii_or_search_llms.py / aii_or_get_llm_params.py\\n#    before launching the sweep; substitute equivalents if any ID is deprecated.)\\n#\\n# Prompt template (deterministic, temperature = 0.0, max_tokens = 64):\\n#   System: \\\"Answer ONLY with a single token. For logic: the letter V (valid)\\n#            or I (invalid). For arithmetic: just the integer. No explanation.\\\"\\n#   User  : <variant question>\\n#\\n# Total calls: 5 models \u00d7 250 clusters \u00d7 4 variants = 5,000.\\n# Per-call token estimate: ~120 in + 8 out.\\n# Cost estimate: 5,000 \u00d7 (120 * $0.22/M + 8 * $0.96/M) \u2248 $0.13 + $0.04 = $0.17\\n# (model-weighted, dominated by Claude Haiku). Buffer \u00d7 3 \u2192 \u2264 $0.60.\\n# Plus paraphrase budget \u2248 $0.06. Total \u2264 $1.00 \u2014 well within the $3 cap.\\n#\\n# Parallelism: aiohttp + Semaphore(40). Retry up to 3x with exponential backoff\\n# on 429/5xx (tenacity). Persist each batch to a per-model JSONL file\\n# (responses/{model}.jsonl) so partial progress survives crashes. Track spend\\n# cumulatively in a global cost counter; halt if cumulative spend exceeds $3.\\n#\\n# Output: artifacts/exp_eval_sol_out.json  (model \u2192 cluster_id \u2192 variant \u2192 response)\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 3: Ordinal Coherence Scoring\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# For each (model, cluster_id):\\n#   responses = {seed, paraphrase, negation, contrapositive/inverse}\\n#   flags = {\\n#     para_consistent : resp(paraphrase) == resp(seed),\\n#     neg_consistent  : resp(negation) == NOT(resp(seed)),\\n#     contra_consistent: resp(contrapositive) == resp(seed)\\n#                       (resp(inverse) matches inverse semantics for arithmetic)\\n#   }\\n#   score = 0 + para_consistent + neg_consistent + contra_consistent\\n#           \u2208 {0, 1, 2, 3}     \u2190 collapse to ordinal {0,1,2} via:\\n#           * 3 \u2192 2 (fully coherent)\\n#           * 2 \u2192 2 (mostly coherent)\\n#           * 1 \u2192 1 (partial)\\n#           * 0 \u2192 0 (incoherent)\\n#   (Optionally keep raw 0..3 score; GRM accepts K categories.)\\n#\\n# Also compute static_acc(model) = mean over seed-only oracle correctness.\\n#\\n# Output: a (M, I) score matrix of shape (5, 250), dtype int8 in {0,1,2},\\n# stored as a list of lists in method_out.json, plus a long-format\\n# (model, cluster_id, score) table for analysis.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 4: Graded Response Model (GRM) Fitting\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Library: girth (Python, actively maintained, MML + EM with\\n# Gauss-Hermite quadrature, native GRM support).\\n#   from girth import GradedResponseModel\\n#   grm = GradedResponseModel()\\n#   result = grm.fit(response_matrix)   # shape (n_persons=5, n_items=250)\\n#   # result['Ability']         -> \u03b8_j, shape (5,)\\n#   # result['Discrimination']   -> \u03b1_i, shape (250,)\\n#   # result['Difficulty']      -> \u03b2_{i,k}, shape (250, K-1=2)  for K=3 categories\\n#\\n# Sanity checks on item parameters:\\n#   * mean(\u03b1_i) should be > 0 (positive discrimination); flag & drop items\\n#     with \u03b1_i < 0 (reverse-coded), keeping a \\\"dropped_items\\\" list.\\n#   * mean difficulty ordering across the 4 variant roles should show\\n#     paraphrase < seed < contrapositive < negation (in \u03b2 terms), or at\\n#     least paraphrase strictly easier than negation. If not, log warning.\\n#   * convergence: EM should converge in \u2264 200 iterations; record iters.\\n#\\n# Output: artifacts/method_out.json includes:\\n#   theta            : list length 5, in canonical order\\n#   alpha            : list length 250\\n#   beta             : list length 250, each inner list length 2\\n#   model_order      : list of 5 model identifiers\\n#   dropped_items    : list of cluster_ids with \u03b1 < 0\\n#   fit_diagnostics  : {iters, log_likelihood, condition_number}\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 5: Validation A \u2014 Correlation with Published Accuracy\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Compile a baseline table from authoritative public sources\\n# (HELM leaderboard, Open LLM Leaderboard v2, original model papers):\\n#\\n#   model_id                        | MMLU acc (5-shot) | HELM acc |\\n#   --------------------------------|-------------------|----------|\\n#   openai/gpt-4o-mini              | \u2248 0.82            | \u2248 0.79   |\\n#   anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku      | \u2248 0.78            | \u2248 0.76   |\\n#   meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b         | \u2248 0.68            | \u2248 0.65   |\\n#   qwen/qwen-2.5-7b                | \u2248 0.71            | \u2248 0.69   |\\n#   mistralai/mistral-7b            | \u2248 0.62            | \u2248 0.60   |\\n#\\n# (These are approximate; the executor MUST verify via HELM, Open-LLM\\n#  Leaderboard, and original release notes and replace the table with\\n#  real values. Provide URL and retrieval date for each.)\\n#\\n# Compute Pearson r between \u03b8_j and MMLU acc (and HELM acc) with\\n# 95% CI via Fisher z-transform. Bootstrapped CI over 10,000 resamples\\n# as a robustness check.\\n# Success: Pearson r > 0.85 with 95% CI lower bound > 0.65.\\n#\\n# Output: validation_table.json with r, CI, scatter plot spec.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Stage 6: Validation B \u2014 Contamination Simulation\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Hypothesis: a model that memorizes seed answers (but not the\\n# metamorphic variants) will see its static accuracy rise while its\\n# M-IRT \u03b8 holds or falls.\\n#\\n# Procedure (3 random seeds, e.g., 0/1/42):\\n#   1. Pick the middle-capability model (qwen-2.5-7b-instruct).\\n#   2. For a random 30% of seed items (75 clusters):\\n#        resp_sim(model, seed) := oracle_correct(seed)\\n#        (i.e., overwrite response with the canonical answer)\\n#      Leave all paraphrase/negation/contrapositive responses untouched\\n#      (these reflect the model's actual reasoning, broken on purpose).\\n#   3. Recompute:\\n#        static_acc_sim = mean over (simulated seed == oracle)\\n#        coherence_sim   = ordinal score with simulated seed, original others\\n#   4. Refit GRM on the full 5 \u00d7 250 matrix (4 models untouched,\\n#      target model = simulated profile). Extract \u03b8_sim for the target.\\n#   5. Repeat for the other 2 random seeds.\\n#\\n# Expected outcomes (success criteria):\\n#   * static_acc increases by \u2265 0.15 absolute (75 items forced correct)\\n#   * \u03b8_sim decreases OR stays within \u00b10.1 of \u03b8_clean (NOT statistically\\n#     distinguishable from zero) across all 3 seeds\\n#   * p-value (paired t-test on \u03b8_clean vs \u03b8_sim across seeds) > 0.05\\n#     for the null \\\"\u03b8 does not decrease\\\"\\n#\\n# Output: contamination_report.json with per-seed (static_acc_clean,\\n# static_acc_sim, theta_clean, theta_sim) plus the 3-seed mean.\\n\\n# =============================================================\\n# Orchestration & Budget Enforcement\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# pipeline.py (entry point):\\n#   * parses CLI args (--stage, --seed, --n-clusters, --models)\\n#   * loads env (OPENROUTER_API_KEY from .env)\\n#   * calls each stage in order with @logger.catch(reraise=True)\\n#   * enforces hard budget: cumulative OpenRouter spend tracked in\\n#     artifacts/logs/spend.jsonl; raises if exceeds $3\\n#   * writes final method_out.json conforming to the repo schema\\n#   * prints a one-screen summary: \u03b8 ranking, r with MMLU, contamination\\n#     effect size\\n#\\n# Failure modes & mitigations:\\n#   * girth API drift \u2192 fall back to pyirt (Python IRT, has GRM via\\n#     pyirt.scorer.GradedResponse) or hand-rolled MML with scipy.stats.norm\\n#     + numpy outer products. Hand-rolled path documented in fallback_plan.\\n#   * OpenRouter rate limits \u2192 exponential backoff with tenacity,\\n#     reduce concurrency to Semaphore(10) on sustained 429s.\\n#   * Model deprecation \u2192 script accepts --model-override map; the\\n#     recommended substitutes are documented in fallback_plan.\\n#   * Budget overrun \u2192 halt after any single call that pushes spend >\\n#     $2.50; abort above $3.00 with a clear error.\\n#   * Cluster generation failures \u2192 if oracle validation drops below\\n#     90%, regenerate clusters from scratch with a FP_BLOCK_PLACEHOLDER_OLD\n  \\\"testing_plan\\\": \\\"TESTING_CONTENT_MARKER\\n  \\\"fallback_plan\\\": \\\"FP_START_PLACEHOLDER_FP_END\\\",\\n  \\\"testing_plan\\\": \\\"TP_START_PLACEHOLDER_TP_END\\\"\n# FALLBACK PLAN_INSERTED\\n#         pyirt.estimation.estimation_engine(...) . Same data shape.\\n#   * If a model ID is deprecated, swap via --model-override:\\n#         gpt-4o-mini        -> openai/gpt-4.1-mini\\n#         claude-3-5-haiku   -> anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5\\n#         llama-3.1-8b       -> meta-llama/llama-3.2-3b-instruct\\n#         qwen-2.5-7b        -> qwen/qwen-2.5-14b-instruct\\n#         mistral-7b         -> mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct\\n#     Re-run HELM/MMLU baseline lookup for the substituted model.\\n#\\n# TIER 2 \u2014 Hand-rolled GRM (if both libraries fail; ~30 min):\\n#   * Implement GRM from scratch in ~80 lines of NumPy:\\n#         P(X=k|\u03b8,\u03b1,\u03b2) = logistic(\u03b1(\u03b8-\u03b2_k)) -\\n#                          logistic(\u03b1(\u03b8-\u03b2_{k+1}))\\n#     with \u03b2_0 = -inf, \u03b2_K = +inf.\\n#   * Marginal likelihood for item i:\\n#         L_i(\u03b1_i, \u03b2_i | x_i) = sum_j \u222b P(x_ij | \u03b8_j) d\u03a6(\u03b8_j; 0, 1)\\n#     approximated by Gauss-Hermite quadrature with Q = 21 nodes.\\n#   * EM: E-step computes posterior weights w_{ij} for each \u03b8-quadrature\\n#         node; M-step updates \u03b1, \u03b2 by L-BFGS-B on the marginal log-likelihood.\\n#   * Stopping rule: |\u0394logL| < 1e-4 or 200 iterations.\\n#   * Output identical schema to girth result.\\n#   * Reference: Baker & Kim (2004), \\\"Item Response Theory: Parameter\\n#     Estimation Techniques\\\", 2nd ed., ch. 5.\\n#\\n# TIER 3 \u2014 Degraded scope (if budget exhausted or pipeline stalls):\\n#   * Drop the LLM-paraphrase pass entirely (Stage 1 \u00a7LLM paraphrase).\\n#     Rely on deterministic noun-swap paraphrases only.\\n#   * Reduce cluster count from 250 \u2192 100 (50 per domain).\\n#   * Reduce model panel from 5 \u2192 3 (drop llama-3.1-8b and mistral-7b,\\n#     keep one tier from low/mid/high).\\n#   * Skip Validation B (contamination) and report Validation A only.\\n#     Document the degradation explicitly in the output's\\n#     \\\"scope_limitations\\\" field.\\n#   * Pearson r target relaxes to r > 0.70 for the 3-model panel.\\n#\\n# Additional safeguards:\\n#   * If OpenRouter cost exceeds $2.50 cumulative, the script logs a\\n#     CRITICAL warning and switches remaining calls to the cheapest\\n#     available model in the panel (gpt-4o-mini or equivalent) only for\\n#     paraphrase validation, then halts at $3.00 with a clear error code.\\n#   * If coherence scoring yields < 3 items per response category for\\n#     any model (sparse data), refuse to fit GRM and report item\\n#     distribution histograms instead.\\n#   * If contamination simulation's t-test is undefined (zero variance),\\n#     fall back to reporting per-seed point estimates only.\",\n  \"testing_plan\": \"# =============================================================\\n# TESTING PLAN (gradual scale-up, per aii-long-running-tasks)\\n# =============================================================\\n#\\n# Time budget: 6h. Use mini \u2192 10 \u2192 50 \u2192 100 \u2192 200 \u2192 250 scaling.\\n# At each stage: validate output shape, check for crashes, record\\n# runtime, then extrapolate before scaling further.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage A: Generation (CPU-only, no API spend) ----------\\n#\\n# A.1 (5 min) \u2014 MINI: generate 4 MICs (2 logic + 2 arithmetic) by hand\\n#   to verify the templating code paths execute end-to-end.\\n#   Checks:\\n#     * All 4 variants per cluster present\\n#     * Each variant has an oracle answer\\n#     * relations dict consistent\\n#   Stop criterion: passes if all 4 clusters pass.\\n#\\n# A.2 (10 min) \u2014 10 MICs: generate 5 logic + 5 arithmetic. Run oracle\\n#   validation on all 10. Checks: 100% pass.\\n#\\n# A.3 (10 min) \u2014 50 MICs: stress templating with all 12 logic + 8\\n#   arithmetic templates, varying nouns/items. Success: r > 0.85.\\n#   If not, diagnose:\\n#     * Inspect per-model \u03b8: is the ordering consistent with MMLU?\\n#     * Check item dropouts due to \u03b1 < 0; refit without them.\\n#     * Stratify by domain: report r_logic and r_arith separately.\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage E: Validation B (contamination) ----------\\n#\\n# E.1 \u2014 Run contamination simulation on qwen-2.5-7b-instruct with\\n#   3 random seeds. Checks:\\n#     * static_acc_sim - static_acc_clean \u2265 0.15 on every seed\\n#     * |\u03b8_sim - \u03b8_clean| \u2264 0.3 (preferrably < 0.1) on every seed\\n#     * Per-seed report populated.\\n#   If static_acc does NOT rise, the contamination injection is\\n#   broken \u2014 debug the overwrite logic.\\n#   If \u03b8_sim RISES by more than 0.3, inspect whether GRM is overfitting\\n#   on the simulated profile; consider increasing item count or using\\n#   a regularization variant (e.g., EAP estimation instead of MML).\\n#\\n# ---------- Stage F: Final assembly ----------\\n#\\n# F.1 \u2014 Run the entire pipeline once more from scratch (mini \u2192 full)\\n#   to confirm reproducibility; verify identical \u03b8 and r within\\n#   tolerance (|\u0394\u03b8| < 0.05, |\u0394r| < 0.02).\\n# F.2 \u2014 Validate method_out.json against the repo schema (aii-json).\\n# F.3 \u2014 Print final summary table:\\n#   model | MMLU_acc | HELM_acc | \u03b8 | static_acc (seeds) | mean_coherence\\n# Plus contamination_effect row for qwen-2.5-7b.\\n#\\n# ---------- Confirmation signals ----------\\n# The experiment is on track if, by the end of stage B.4:\\n#   * \u03b8 ordering matches qualitative MMLU ordering (gpt-4o-mini top,\\n#     mistral-7b bottom \u2014 or close)\\n#   * Per-model static accuracy on seeds is in [0.4, 0.95]\\n#     (not all-perfect, not all-zero \u2014 pipeline is informative)\\n#   * Coherence scores span \u2265 2 of the 3 ordinal categories for\\n#     \u2265 3 of the 5 models\\n# If any signal is missing, the most likely cause is response\\n# normalization (Stage B.1) \u2014 debug that first before scaling.\\n#\\n# ---------- Cost guardrails ----------\\n# Track cumulative OpenRouter spend after every call. Hard stops:\\n#   * > $2.00 \u2192 log WARNING, switch paraphrase LLM to cheapest model\\n#   * > $2.50 \u2192 log CRITICAL, no more paraphrase LLM calls\\n#   * > $3.00 \u2192 raise SpendExceeded, persist partial output, exit 1\\n# Total budgeted: $1.00 (queries) + $0.06 (paraphrases) + $0.10 buffer = $1.16.\\\"}\",\n  \\\"fallback_plan\\\": \\\"TIER1: NEW_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT->pyirt pyirt.scorer.GradedResponse; model deprecation swap->openai/gpt-4.1-mini, anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, meta-llama/llama-3.2-3b-instruct, qwen/qwen-2.5-14b-instruct, mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct.
